brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases stacked on levels 0 and 1: full base piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1, plus half-e pieces at (1,0,0) and (1,0,1) and half-n pieces at (0,-1,0) and (0,-1,1). Overall about 334 x 160 x 418 mm.
Two drawers, drawer:0#0,-1#cut (level 0) and drawer:1#0,-1#cut (level 1), sit on the cut faces of the two half-n bases.
Sized to a footprint of about 334 x 418 mm and 160 mm tall; I could not check it against a specific bench. Nothing was placed in a work-clear zone, but no bench fit was verified.

requirements.requirement: House rules: close open faces with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces was refused with MESH_CLASH: the solid end caps would run into the drawer frames (4.5 mm overlap). Caps were not applied, so 24 open faces remain (reported as OPEN_CAP_FACE info). lockJoints made no change because nothing needed locking.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex tower of 6 base pieces with two drawers, one on each level, on the north-half bases. check_build reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. The house-rule capOpenFaces was refused because it clashes with the drawer frames, so the open faces are uncapped; I did not force a workaround. Fit to a specific workbench was not verified.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
